To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT FOR REVIEW — Stop using Brightline Pro 6% batch LX2291

DRAFT ONLY — not to go up until I’ve read it over.

Everyone, please check your developer before your next colour. Kelvin Trade have confirmed a filling error affecting Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L, batch LX2291. Bottles labelled 6% may actually contain 12% (40 vol) — twice the strength on the label. This is a safety issue, not just an inconvenience.

WHICH BOTTLES TO CHECK

The affected batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026. I bought mine off the Kelvin Trade rep on 28 October.

Check the batch code on the BASE OF EACH BOTTLE. It’s not on the box, so checking the outer packaging isnae enough. Check open bottles in your trolley as well as unopened stock in the back. Please make sure anyone renting here who buys from the same rep sees this.

If the base says LX2291, stop using it immediately. Put it aside, clearly marked “DO NOT USE”, somewhere nobody can pick it up by mistake. If the code is missing or unreadable, keep it out of use until Kelvin Trade can confirm what it is. Don’t try to judge the strength by looking at it, testing it on someone or diluting it yourself.

Kelvin Trade say other batches and other strengths are not affected.

WHAT’S HAPPENED AND WHAT IT CAN DO

On Saturday a client had burning and red patches on their scalp during a bleach retouch using a new bottle from this batch. The lift was much faster than usual. I stopped and rinsed as soon as they reported burning. No client details are being shared here.

There’s also been a report here of unusually hot foils and very fast lift using the same batch on Thursday. That was initially put down to the heater. We can’t establish every cause from those reports, but don’t dismiss unexpected heat as just the heater.

Stronger developer can make a mix more aggressive than intended, causing rapid or uneven lift, dryness, damage and breakage, as well as scalp irritation or chemical burns. A normal-looking mix or a previous patch test does not make a wrongly labelled bottle safe. Don’t wait for unusual lift or heat before taking this batch out of use.

IF SOMEONE REACTS IN THE CHAIR

Stop the service immediately. Burning, unexpected heat or increasing discomfort is not something to leave developing.

For a suspected chemical burn, follow the salon’s NHS first-aid reference:
• Call 999 for medical help immediately. Don’t wait for blistering or severe pain.
• Protect yourself with gloves. Carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible.
• Rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about one hour. Follow the call handler’s instructions.
• Don’t use shampoo, creams, aloe, neutralisers or other chemicals on it, and don’t carry on with colour or toner.
• Chemical burns need hospital assessment. Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also means 999 immediately.

Once immediate care is underway, record what happened in the incident book and keep client details private. Keep dated notes and, with consent, photos, plus the product name, batch, mixing ratio and timings.

RETURNS — KEEP EVIDENCE FIRST

The rep is in Tuesday, or bottles can go back to Kelvin Trade’s Hillington depot for full credit.

If you’ve had a problem, keep the bottle involved, with any remaining contents, safely set aside as evidence. Don’t bin it or hand it back with the routine returns before agreeing evidence arrangements with your insurer or whoever is investigating. Keep photos of the label and batch code, purchase details and the supplier email too.

Please check every bottle before using any more of this stock.

Kirsty
